mix.rule: per-step cumulative allocation floor((step+1)*steps*batch*share) - floor(step*steps*batch*share) S1 rows; per-sample loss weight 1.0; the batch order is shuffled per step, so the mix is the only source signal

metrics.confusion_matrix_orientation: rows = target action, columns = predicted action

label_rule.note: chosen one-hot CE only; the other 17 logits appear solely in the softmax denominator

gpu.peak_memory_note: torch.cuda.max_memory_{allocated,reserved} over this run; reset immediately before the first step

rollout_checkpoint.note: the checkpoint the beta=0.5 round-2 shards were rolled out from; it equals the WP05.5 50k B0 step-1000 checkpoint, so the data was collected by the beta=1.0 50k student

commands.result: 15/15 complete=true, 3,500 decisions / 7,000 frames each, beta=0.5, stage 0, difficulty normal, stop_reason decisions

commands.step: convert 15 shards with the WP05.2 CLI
independently verify converted labels (rows + SHA-256 + counts)
train B0, 5,000 steps (everything else identical to WP05.7)
dev wiring dry run (60 frames, 1 seed; not evidence)
20 dev episodes after the G410-1 chunk4 teacher batch exited
commands.waited_for: G410-1 chunk4 (tools/rl/v410_teacher_fast20.py, seeds 61375-61399) to exit; polled every 60 s, cap 2400 s; the teacher process was never signalled

window_alignment.training_window: the D410-S1 shards store frames[t-3..t], four consecutive game frames; one decision = two frames = two renders, so the stack is consecutive

actions.note: pooled over the arm's episodes; descriptive only

verdict.what_this_is: smoke: the v410 checkpoint ran in the real engine under the S1N dev ruler

teacher_gate.what: G410-1 chunk4 teacher batch (tools/rl/v410_teacher_fast20.py, seeds 61375-61399, engine rl_laser) that the dev episodes had to wait for
teacher_gate.evals_started_after: the wait loop polls `pgrep -f v410_teacher_fast20` every 60 s and only proceeds once the teacher process is gone
teacher_gate.note: the teacher batch is not this work package's evidence: it is only the reason the 20 episodes were scheduled after it, so that they would not be CPU-starved the way the WP05.7 attempt-1 eval was

fail_closed.check: eval header checkpoint sha256 == train checkpoint sha256
every episode engine_sha256 == eval header engine sha256
recomputed frames mean/median match the evaluator (1e-6)
recomputed idle share matches the evaluator exactly
newline-separated label rows, labels/obs SHA-256 verified per shard (verify_labels.py re-hashed every labels_v410.jsonl)
the first 1,000 steps replay the WP05.7 run's logged losses exactly

verification.note: the builder aborts with exit 3 on any disagreement, so a partial or stale eval JSON cannot be promoted into this file

comparison.rule: descriptive side-by-side only: the beta=0.5 1k arm shares this run's shards, labels, mix, optimiser, seed and dev suite, so the only controlled change is 5x budget (128,000 -> 640,000 samples); the beta=1.0 50k arm differs in the injection coefficient and the rollout student. No interval, no significance test, no gate, no decision rule
confounds: the only deliberate change versus the 1k arm is the step budget: 1,000 -> 5,000 steps (128,000 -> 640,000 samples over the same 46,397 S1 rows and 52,500 DAgger rows); data, mix, seed, optimiser and dev suite are identical
one training seed (0) and one checkpoint per arm: no variance estimate

the beta=1.0 50k arm was collected at injection_rate 1.0 and rolled out from the round-1 baseline 3bc0ec44..., while the beta=0.5 shards were rolled out from 6ebe4ea9... at injection_rate 0.500857, so the beta=1.0 contrast is not a controlled budget comparison
this run trained while the G410-1 chunk4 teacher batch (6 concurrent teacher instances) shared the same host, exactly as the 1k arm did

scope.purpose: WP05.8 controlled budget follow-up to WP05.7: B0 behaviour cloning on the same 15 complete beta=0.5 round-2 DAgger shards, 5,000 steps instead of 1,000, plus the 20 descriptive dev episodes
scope.game_launched_note: only by tools/rl/v410_student_eval.py for the 20 dev episodes; no collection rollout was run

tool_payload_note: touhou_rl/v410/dagger/train.py embeds a generic WP05.3 smoke scope/not_claimed block in train_run.json (it still says '1,000 steps', 'not a beta=0.5 round'). That text is stale for this run; it is preserved verbatim under raw_tool_payload_scope below and is NOT relied on for any claim here.

not_claimed: not the 50k-decision first DAgger round: this smoke trains 1,000 steps on the six completed shards (21,000 decisions, ~42 % of the 50k target)
not a β=0.5 round: every shard here used β=1.0 (full teacher injection)
not G410-2: no confirm-split run, no 20-episode protocol, no four-arm matrix
not a development score: the offline metrics are in-sample on the exact train batches this run consumed, so they are optimisation diagnostics, not held-out skill
no new data collection and no engine run: the game is never launched by this module; the two dev episodes are a separate evaluator invocation
one model arm (B0), one seed (0), one fixed step budget (1,000): no variance estimate and no convergence claim
rows without a chosen plan are excluded, and unknown candidates are never negative labels; that rule is not a learned preference over unknowns
G410-2 (the v4.1.0 acceptance gate) -- not measured, not attempted
any significance test, confidence interval or pass/fail gate on the 20 dev episodes: the contrast with the 1k and beta=1.0 arms is descriptive
that 5,000 steps fixes, improves or is sufficient for S1N clearance: 0/20 clears on every arm in the comparison
that beta=0.5 data is better or worse than beta=1.0: the two arms differ in the injection coefficient and the rollout student as well as in budget
any RL/PPO training: B0 is behaviour cloning with chosen one-hot CE
that more steps would keep helping: only 1,000 and 5,000 steps were measured
any held-out offline accuracy: every offline metric is in-sample on the exact train batches the run consumed
any new data collection, seed confirmation or teacher re-run

deterministic_continuation.claim: with the same seed, data and mix, the 5,000-step run replays the WP05.7 1,000-step run exactly for its first 1,000 steps, so the only difference between the two checkpoints is the extra 4,000 steps
deterministic_continuation.note: the trainer logs step 1 and then every 100th step, so 11 points inside the first 1,000 steps are comparable; all 11 are bit-identical

limits: one arm (B0), one training seed (0), one budget pair (1k vs 5k): no variance estimate, so a single 20-episode contrast cannot separate budget from noise
52,500 round-2 decisions (105 % of the 50,000 target) but still one DAgger round; 5,000 steps reuse the same 46,397 S1 / 52,500 DAgger rows, so the extra budget is repetition, not new data
offline metrics are in-sample train-batch metrics, not held-out accuracy
dev episodes are the 20 dev seeds only (1000-1019); G410-2 is not measured
wall times are not comparable with the beta=1.0 runs: a G410-1 teacher chunk4 batch (6 concurrent teacher instances) ran on the same 20-core host during training
the dev episodes started only after the chunk4 teacher batch exited, so the eval wall time is comparable with the WP05.7 attempt-2 eval, not with the contended attempt-1
